style_lock: Painterly graphic-novel illustration, visible brushwork, rich colour, slightly caricatured; keep exactly this painted look throughout, never photographic. Faces, masks, fur, costumes and props stay as in the image. No text, no speech balloons, no captions.
settings: Kling 4.0, Keyframes, first frame only, 1080p, adaptive ratio, 1 output

shots.prompt: The red-caped ape brandishes the small paper packet and shakes it as he rants; the grey-maned ape in the cream coat answers with a calm, dry shrug; the maroon-jacketed ape sits hunched and miserable, hugging his stomach. Locked camera. The red-caped ape says: "Ten times the caffeine! I've been awake all bloody night!" The cream-coated ape says: "Yes. I spotted that after you went to bed."

The maroon-jacketed ape grimaces, shifts on his chair and clutches his stomach; the cream-coated ape glances at him sideways. Locked camera. The maroon-jacketed ape says, strained: "I need the toilet."

The plumber in blue overalls at the open door hefts his red toolbox and turns to go out; the maroon-jacketed ape stands hunched and answers faintly; the red-caped ape slumps in the armchair. Locked camera. The plumber says: "Toilet's disconnected. Five minutes." The maroon-jacketed ape says, faintly: "I can do five minutes."

The red-caped ape in the armchair sags, his eyelids droop, his head lolls, and he falls asleep. Slow push in. The red-caped ape says, fading: "I've never been so tired in my life. I feel like I'm gonna pass out."

Exterior. A vast transparent soap-film bubble swells up from the house and settles over the whole ivy-covered cottage and garden, rainbow colours rippling slowly across its surface. Through the ground-floor window the red-caped ape sleeps in his armchair. Outside the bubble the plumber in blue overalls stands frozen mid-reach at the pipe, utterly still, as if time has stopped for him. Very slow camera drift. No dialogue; a soft shimmering hum.

The ape in the steel helmet presses both palms on the glowing bubble wall in the doorway and strains; the wall flexes like elastic under his hands but holds. Behind him the maroon-jacketed ape and the cream-coated ape watch, exhausted; the red-caped ape sleeps in the chair. Outside, beyond the bubble, the plumber stays frozen. Locked camera. The maroon-jacketed ape says: "That's been a bloody long five minutes." The cream-coated ape says: "It hasn't started."

The cream-coated ape plants both hands on the helmeted ape's back and shoves; the helmeted ape strains forward, the bubble wall bulges outward around his palms and springs back; a small, short squeak. Locked camera. The cream-coated ape says: "One good push!"

All three apes recoil: the maroon-jacketed ape claps a hand over his nose and mouth, the cream-coated ape grimaces and waves the air, the helmeted ape hunches, sheepish, and glances back guiltily. The red-caped ape sleeps on behind them. Locked camera. The maroon-jacketed ape says, muffled: "My God. What's that smell?"
